assumptions.statement: English 'righteousness' is an acceptable umbrella term for a starter comparative archive, even though no exact identity across traditions is assumed.
assumptions.repair: Demote the umbrella if later work shows translation distortions are too severe.

assumptions.statement: A small starter source set is enough to ground rev0002 without pretending to exhaustive coverage.
assumptions.repair: Expand only where a concrete open question requires it.

assumptions.statement: The provided reference datacubes are best used as machinery templates rather than as direct substantive authorities on righteousness.
assumptions.repair: Revise the transfer ledger if a stronger borrowing becomes necessary.

assumptions.statement: A compact office theory can be responsibly built from public reason, special obligation, legitimacy, and corruption materials without yet requiring a full theory of the state.
assumptions.repair: Split office theory into narrower role families if later work shows the current public-office compression is too coarse.

assumptions.statement: A portable core / sacred-thickening distinction clarifies the archive better than either strict secular reduction or full theological inseparability.
assumptions.repair: Demote the distinction if later comparative work shows the portable core is too thin to count as righteousness in key traditions.

assumptions.statement: Typed recognition status plus public-translation status is a better way to discipline portability claims than forcing a single yes-or-no verdict on whether the portable core is righteousness proper.
assumptions.repair: Collapse or revise the status scheme if later comparative work shows the distinction is too coarse or unstable.

assumptions.statement: A threshold-band view better captures righteousness than either reducing it to bare permissibility or inflating it into universal heroism.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the threshold-band if later tradition-specific work shows that the floor/ceiling relation varies too much to support a common canon rule.

assumptions.statement: A breach-responsive repair rule compresses the archive better than either making repair always-on or treating it as external to righteousness once wrong has occurred.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the rule if later work shows some traditions keep repair wholly outside righteousness or make it fully constitutive at all times.

assumptions.statement: A standing-sensitive defeater model clarifies righteousness better than treating all defects as additive penalties inside a single balancing score.
assumptions.repair: Demote or refine the model if later work shows that some traditions treat hypocrisy, necessity, or complicity as evidentiary defects only rather than as presumptive disqualifiers.

assumptions.statement: A requalification model clarifies righteousness better than either permanent moral taint or instant restoration through confession, apology, or softer rhetoric.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the model if later work shows some traditions make taint effectively permanent or treat repentance as more immediately standing-restorative than this archive allows.

assumptions.statement: A contestability rule clarifies public righteousness better than treating office as assessable by private virtue alone.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the rule if later work shows some public domains require forms of warranted opacity that cannot be captured by the archive's current review-and-record substitutes.

assumptions.statement: A conflict-and-remainder model clarifies righteousness better than either one-rule moral clean wins or the view that hard conflict dissolves righteous judgment altogether.
assumptions.repair: Demote or refine the model if later work shows that some traditions need a sharper lexical order or, conversely, reject portable priority cues altogether.

assumptions.statement: A temporal model distinguishing episode, standing, and trajectory clarifies righteousness better than either one-shot verdicts or permanent essence labels.
assumptions.repair: Demote or refine the model if later work shows that some traditions or offices collapse these temporal levels more tightly than this archive now allows.

assumptions.statement: A compact righteousness theory should include epistemic burdens under uncertainty rather than treating factual uncertainty, credibility distortion, and revisability as external to righteousness itself.
assumptions.repair: Demote or refine the rule if later work shows some traditions treat uncertainty primarily as a prudential or procedural issue rather than as part of righteous standing.

assumptions.statement: A delegation-discipline rule clarifies righteousness better than either treating proxy action as standing-neutral or demanding undelegated personal control in every serious case.
assumptions.repair: Demote or refine the rule if later work shows some domains require stronger nondelegation constraints or, conversely, treat delegated procedure as more normatively self-standing than this archive allows.

assumptions.statement: A compact equity rule clarifies righteousness better than either rigid rule formalism or unbounded case-by-case discretion.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the rule if later work shows some traditions collapse equity into mercy or practical wisdom, or if offices require more domain-specific guardrails than a portable canon surface can honestly supply.

assumptions.statement: A disciplined interruption rule clarifies righteousness better than either loyal compliance under compromised power or romanticized resistance that treats refusal itself as self-justifying.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the rule if later work shows some domains require stronger presumptions for staying-with-repair, or conversely tighter presumptions against disclosure, resignation, or public breach than this starter canon allows.

assumptions.statement: A compact mercy-and-sanction rule clarifies righteousness better than treating punishment as proof of seriousness or mercy as a free-standing humane good.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the rule if later work shows stronger tradition-specific divergence about whether mercy is a virtue, a pardon power, an equity function, or a victim-side practice, or if public-office and interpersonal cases require separate canon surfaces.

assumptions.statement: A qualified public-trust / nonownership rule clarifies righteous office better than either treating office as privately ownable leverage or collapsing every public role into a literal private-law fiduciary relation.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the rule if later work shows some offices need a stronger fiduciary theory or, conversely, that public-trust vocabulary obscures democratic or constitutional features more than it clarifies them.

assumptions.statement: For public power, bearer, competence, and authorization are not merely legal side-constraints but part of righteous standing itself; when these are missing, the better classification is usually usurpation, interruption, or burdened overreach rather than righteous office-performance.
assumptions.scope: public office, institutional action, delegated public power
assumptions.risk: The rule may be stated too strictly for genuine emergencies, informal constitutional practice, or domains where competence and jurisdiction are distributed across overlapping bearers.
assumptions.next_test: Refine emergency and overlap cases without letting necessity or ambiguity become a solvent for bearer-discipline.

assumptions.statement: A compact affected-standing rule clarifies public righteousness better than treating contestability, testimony, or benevolent intent as sufficient even when those most burdened were not seriously heard or represented.
assumptions.repair: Demote or refine the rule if later work shows some domains justifiably rely more heavily on authorized surrogates, expert guardianship, or post hoc review than this starter canon presently allows.

assumptions.statement: A compact absent-claimant rule clarifies righteousness better than either treating direct present voice as the only serious form of standing or allowing proxies to overwrite the claimant in the name of care.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the rule if later work shows children, supported decision-making, diffuse publics, and future generations need more sharply different standards than a single canon surface can carry.

assumptions.statement: A bounded-partiality rule clarifies righteousness better than either flat impartiality or unrestricted loyalty, while leaving room for role-sensitive differences between intimate care, representation, and impartial public office.
assumptions.repair: Demote or split the rule if later work shows that family, constituency, covenantal, and office cases require more sharply distinct canons than one starter surface can honestly carry.
